sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark
sources.evidence: Reopened the complete announcement text on October 27, 2026. February 12 research preview explicitly calls Spark a smaller version of GPT-5.3-Codex; text-only, 128K, Cerebras serving and over 1,000 tokens/s, but no total or activated parameter count. This size-changing relationship does not support inheriting the parent model count. The prior audit could not inspect original chart labels after direct HTML/browser challenges; this pass inspected article text only.

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark Powered by Cerebras
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The February 12 hardware-partner announcement calls Spark a smaller Codex version and reports throughput, but no total or active parameter count. Trillion-parameter support describes future-capable Cerebras infrastructure, not Spark size.

sources.title: Codex changelog: Spark launch and retirement
sources.evidence: Full changelog downloaded and searched for exact Spark references. February 12 launch entry specifies text-only 128K; September 14, 2026 entry retires the research preview from the desktop app, CLI and IDE extension. No intervening Spark capability expansion was found in these entries. Public API access was unavailable at launch; private design-partner access in the announcement is a different scope.

sources.title: Models: deprecated Codex models
sources.evidence: Current model guide confirms Spark retired September 14, 2026 from Codex product surfaces. General reasoning controls describe available models; this does not independently establish retired Spark reasoning support.

sources.title: OpenAI Models at Ultrafast Speed
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Later partnership comparison explicitly names GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark alongside GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast. Reports Spark throughput above 1,000 tokens/s but no numerical parameter count, activated-count convention or neural architecture. Historical preview language does not override OpenAI retirement documentation.

sources.title: Speeding up agentic workflows with WebSockets in the Responses API
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. April 22 engineering account identifies Spark in the production Codex Responses API tool-execution loop and WebSocket mode, but reports no parameter counts. Its caching of API response state, tokenization and routing does not establish model attention or KV caching.

sources.title: All models
sources.evidence: Fresh original API catalog fetched October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200) and searched in full. Spark is absent; no Spark model specification or weights are supplied. Separately identifies gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b as Apache-licensed open-weight models.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited hosted-service access and reserve service intellectual-property rights. Supports descriptive proprietary classification for hosted Spark, not a downloadable weight license.

sources.title: Attempted exact Spark API model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-path request on October 27, 2026 returned HTTP 404. No Spark total or active count can be recovered from this unavailable API model card.

sources.title: Stop Shipping AI Slop: How Codex Spark Changes The Way You Code
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. March 4 Spark-specific usage guide reports 128K context and tool-based workflows including edits, tests and review, with no numerical total or active parameters, neural architecture, or exact-model reasoning-effort specification.

sources.title: GPT-5.3-Codex System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the original February 5 system card and searched the freshly fetched full PDF text on October 27, 2026. It covers the named GPT-5.3-Codex parent, with safety/benchmark sections but no numerical total or activated parameter specification and no Spark entry. It supplies no count to combine with the launch relationship; Spark is explicitly smaller, so unchanged-size lineage would also be unsupported.

name.note: Use the developer’s exact model name.

developer.note: Cerebras supplies inference hardware; OpenAI develops the model.

family.note: Normalize the generation; Spark is a smaller GPT-5.3-Codex variant.

release_date.note: Earliest announced public research preview. February 5 belongs to full GPT-5.3-Codex.

open_weights.note: Hosted proprietary release; no Spark weight distribution identified.

license.note: Descriptive model-access classification, not an SPDX weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened original OpenAI/Cerebras announcements, later partner comparison and usage guide, engineering account, current API catalog and named-parent system card. None supplies a nominal Spark total. OpenAI explicitly describes a smaller model, so an unchanged parent-size inference fails. Bounded exact-name later disclosure searches found no developer count; throughput-derived estimates are not published specifications.

active_parameters_b.note: No separate Spark active-parameter count or counting convention appears in the reopened primary sources. Fresh exact-name searches for later technical reports and explicit active-parameter comparisons found no qualifying original model-team table. Throughput-based estimates do not establish active weights, and no dense total-to-active equality is assumed.

architecture.note: Consulted original and later primary materials disclose serving hardware and API architecture, not the neural architecture. Exact-name training/interpretability searches found no model-structure disclosure. WebSocket state caching is not sufficient Transformer evidence.

context_window.note: 128K in the launch and March usage guide; last documented limit located before retirement, not a live endpoint test.

modalities.note: Text-only specification; no later documented multimodal expansion found. Clear unsupported image/PDF inputs.

reasoning.note: Exact-model reasoning capability could not be verified from accessible primary text. A secondary chart description identifies Spark reasoning efforts, but the original chart labels were inaccessible (direct HTML 403; browser challenge). Generic Codex controls and sibling capabilities are insufficient. Clear the flag to null pending primary chart verification; null does not mean no reasoning.

tool_call.note: Spark is documented in the Codex tool-execution loop, including edits and tests; no claim about every standalone API tool.

patch.notes: Research preview released February 12, 2026; retired from Codex desktop, CLI and IDE on September 14, 2026. Last documented specifications found are text-only and 128K context. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; the smaller-model relationship to GPT-5.3-Codex supplies no numerical size. Neural architecture remains undisclosed. Dedicated reasoning support remains unverified; this does not establish absence of reasoning. Exact API model documentation returned 404. Private design-partner API access at launch does not establish general API availability.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening original/later primary sources and searching later exact-model disclosures and active-count comparisons. The smaller GPT-5.3-Codex relationship cannot supply an unchanged-size inference; hardware capacity and throughput estimates are not model counts. Preserve the other 12 assessments and original launch, modality, reasoning and retirement corrections.
